latest_release.body:
# Surya v0.24.0 — Zero-PyTorch Lightweight Architecture, Interactive Web Viewer (`surya_gui`) & Agent-Ready CLI

Surya `0.24.0` completes the transition to **Surya 2.5** (`datalab-to/surya-ocr-2.5`) — our 689M-parameter vision-language model for **full-page & per-block OCR**, **layout analysis & reading order**, **inline & block LaTeX math (`<math>`)**, and **HTML table recognition (`<table>` with `colspan` / `rowspan`)** across 90+ languages:

- **85.9 on [OmniParseBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/datalab-to/omni_parse_bench)** (highest of any open model under 1B parameters) and **83.7% on [olmOCR-bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/olmOCR-bench)**.
- **4.5 pages/s on a single H100** at 192 DPI (`6.2 pages/s` at 96 DPI) — **1.7× faster than Surya 2** and **3.2× faster on Apple Silicon (`llama.cpp` Metal)** because compact block headers (`<|Label|><|x0|><|y0|><|x1|><|y1|>`) and compact table tokens cut output tokens per page by **62%**.
- **Zero Heavy ML Dependencies (`pip install surya-ocr` installs in seconds)** — removed `torch`, `torchvision`, `transformers`, `opencv-python-headless`, and `streamlit` from runtime dependencies (`>10,000` lines of legacy v1/RF-DETR code removed). Surya now runs as a lightweight client/orchestrator over **`vllm`** (Docker or Podman), **`llama.cpp`** (`llama-server` / `llama-cli`), or **`mlx-vlm`** (Apple Silicon).
- **New Built-In Interactive Web Viewer (`surya_gui`)** — zero-extra-dependency browser UI to inspect layout boxes, reading order, KaTeX-typeset math, HTML tables, and JSON page by page across all Surya modes.

> Need handwriting, complex forms, or managed VLM parsing at scale with zero infrastructure? Try **[Chandra on the Datalab API](https://www.datalab.to/?utm_source=gh-surya-release)** — get **5,000 free pages every month** when you sign up with a work email.

---

## 1. Built-In Interactive Web Viewer (`surya_gui`)

`surya_gui` now launches a fast, self-contained web viewer directly from the standard library (no `streamlit` installation required):

```bash
surya_gui --port 8000
```

- Drag & drop any **PDF** or **image** (`PNG`, `JPG`, `WEBP`, `GIF`, `TIFF`, `BMP`).
- Switch live between **Full-Page OCR**, **Block OCR** (96 DPI layout + 192 DPI block crops), **Layout**, and **Table Recognition**.
- Interactive SVG overlays for **layout bounding boxes**, **canonical block labels**, and **reading order** with bidirectional hover highlighting between the page canvas and the `Blocks` tab.
- Inspect **Preview** (with live KaTeX math rendering and styled HTML tables), **Blocks**, **HTML**, and **JSON**, with one-click `Copy HTML` and `.json` download.

---

## 2. Clean Top-Level Python API & New Predictor Capabilities

```python
from PIL import Image
from surya import (
    LayoutPredictor,
    RecognitionPredictor,
    SuryaInferenceManager,
    TableRecPredictor,
)

manager = SuryaInferenceManager()  # auto-spawns vllm (GPU) or llama-server (CPU / Apple Silicon)
image = Image.open("page.png").convert("RGB")

# 1. Full-page OCR (default: one VLM call per page -> blocks, bboxes, reading order, HTML + <math>)
rec = RecognitionPredictor(manager)
pages = rec([image])

# Optional: pass skip_labels=[] to also OCR text inside Figure / Picture / Diagram regions
pages_with_figures = rec([image], skip_labels=[])

# 2. Two-stage Layout + Block-mode OCR (auto-runs LayoutPredictor if layouts not passed)
block_pages = rec([image], full_page=False)

# 3. HTML Table Recognition (<table> with colspan / rowspan)
tables = TableRecPredictor(manager)([image])
print(tables[0].html)
```

### What's New in the Predictors & Backends
- **Top-level package exports**: Import `SuryaInferenceManager`, `get_default_manager`, `LayoutPredictor`, `RecognitionPredictor`, `TableRecPredictor`, and `__version__` directly from `surya`.
- **Configurable `skip_labels` (`#544`)**: Pass `skip_labels=[]` (or a custom set of labels) to `RecognitionPredictor` to OCR text inside `Figure`, `Picture`, or `Diagram
